finding.claim: data: URI mediatype fallback: a mediatype that fails DATA_URI_MEDIATYPE (e.g. 'text/html/x') is mapped to 'text/plain', which is allowlisted, so the URL is allowed. If a browser parses that mediatype as text/html, the data-type allowlist is bypassed. Exploitability is UNCERTAIN: the browser MIME parse was not verified (WebFetch permission denied), and top-level data: navigation is blocked in mainstream browsers.
finding.source: attribute value of an allowed URI attribute (href/src/action/cite/poster/preload/longdesc/xlink:href/xml:base) in attacker HTML, via Loofah.html5_fragment/html4_fragment scrub!(:strip/:prune/:escape)
finding.sink: serialized attribute value emitted to the browser

trace.note: data_uri_mediatype returns the raw mediatype only if it matches DATA_URI_MEDIATYPE
non-matching mediatype (e.g. text/html/x, which has two slashes) returns 'text/plain'

finding.guards_checked: Control-character stripping and entity decoding run before the check (scrub.rb:172-175). Protocol allowlist enforced (scrub.rb:178). Mediatype check's return value is used (scrub.rb:182). The fallback to text/plain is the weak point. Browser MIME parsing not verified.

finding.claim: CSS url() nested inside an allowlisted function survives sanitization. The url filter only inspects direct children of a property, so 'background-image: linear-gradient(url(http://attacker/x), red)' keeps the inner url, and the browser fetches the attacker URL. Impact is remote resource load/tracking, not script execution; this contradicts the documented sanitize_css behavior (helpers.rb:31).
finding.source: style attribute value in attacker HTML (scrub_css_attribute) or string passed to Loofah::Helpers.sanitize_css
finding.sink: re-serialized CSS property emitted into the style attribute / returned string

trace.note: scrub_css_attribute passes style value to scrub_css
url_flags filter checks only direct children of the property node
background-image passes via SHORTHAND_CSS_PROPERTIES check on name.split('-').first
allowed :function child is kept, not inspected
sanitized tree is stringified and emitted

finding.guards_checked: Top-level url/bad_url filter (scrub.rb:104-106) works for direct children. Function-name allowlist (scrub.rb:122) works. Nested url inside an allowed function is not filtered. Crass parse-tree shape inferred from usage; the crass gem is not in the repo and was not read.

finding.claim: Local-only href restriction for SVG elements does not apply to textPath under the HTML5 (gumbo) parser, because the gumbo-adjusted tag name 'textPath' is not in SVG_ALLOW_LOCAL_HREF (only lowercase 'textpath' is). A remote href on textPath is kept. Low impact: remote reference only. href still passes allowed_uri?, so javascript: is blocked. Html4 (libxml2, lowercased names) is not affected.
finding.source: attacker HTML <textPath href='http://attacker/…'> parsed via Loofah.html5_fragment/html5_document
finding.sink: serialized SVG href attribute emitted to the browser

trace.note: downcased variants are added, so 'textPath' is never added
href is in ATTR_VAL_IS_URI, so allowed_uri? still applies

finding.guards_checked: allowed_uri? still blocks javascript:/vbscript: on href. Only the local-reference restriction is bypassed. Tag-name casing from gumbo (textPath) is inferred from the HTML5 spec, not run.
